title: Motor Imagery vs Rest - Low-Cost EEG System
description: EEG recordings from 10 BCI-naive participants acquired with a low-cost consumer-grade device during a motor imagery versus rest protocol. Participants performed kinesthetic imagination of a grasping movement with the dominant hand and rest/idle conditions across five runs, including an initial real-movement run. EMG of the dominant hand was recorded for protocol control, supporting evaluation of affordable brain-computer interface systems.
methods_description: EEG was recorded with a low-cost consumer-grade device (15 channels, 125 Hz sampling, left earlobe reference) and filtered online between 0.5 and 45 Hz with a 3rd-order Butterworth bandpass filter. RUN0 involved real grasping to familiarize participants; RUN1-RUN4 consisted of motor imagery versus rest trials. Dominant-hand EMG was acquired for protocol control.
